summary: Re-tested the iteration_3 auth fixes and the move to Bearer tokens. Backend: 51/51 pytest pass: the 45 existing tests plus 6 new ones in tests/test_auth_fixes.py covering the XFF bypass, the per-email lock, the TTL index, link-info for a deleted employee, Bearer login and refresh by body, and the CORS preflight from the 1c87 host. In the first run 1 test failed: TestInactive was fragile because it relied on another class running first under xdist. I made it self-contained (test-only change). Frontend: on BOTH hosts (1c87bdcc... where the frontend and API hosts differ, and the REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL host) these work: login (wrong password shows an error), reload keeps the session, sign out goes to /login and erm_session is removed from localStorage, and the session stays signed out after reload. The 'Network Error' from iteration_3 is gone. Silent refresh works (tested on the 1c87 host, where no cookies are sent): with access_token removed, or set to garbage, the app calls /auth/refresh, saves a new access_token and stays signed in. With both tokens invalid it clears storage and goes to /login. Set-password link flow: key icon -> link dialog -> new browser context -> mismatch error -> success, then signed in. Change password: the confirm field and the mismatch toast work; wrong current password, weak password and success toasts all appear; the session survives a reload after the change; the old password is rejected and the new one works.

minor.issue: The cookie is read BEFORE the Authorization header. When the frontend and API are on the same origin (the REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL host in preview, or a same-domain deployment), the browser sends the httpOnly cookie automatically, and it overrides the Bearer token. An explicit Bearer header should win.

The frontend no longer needs cookies, but login, refresh and change-password still set SameSite=None cookies, and current_member still accepts them. With CORS_ORIGINS='*', origin_guard is turned off, so a cross-site request can still carry the user's cookies (CSRF). Consider removing the cookie fallback, or at least setting CORS_ORIGINS explicitly in production.

Behind the ingress, request.client.host is always the proxy pod IP (seen: 10.64.128.135), so the ip+email key acts the same as the email key. The per-email lock also lets anyone lock a known user (including the owner/admin) out for 15 min by sending 5 bad passwords. This is a known trade-off; consider showing the remaining lock time or adding an admin unlock.
The 'identifier' index is not unique, so concurrent upserts could create duplicate rows (low impact).

integration_issues.issue: Any refresh failure, including a network error or a 5xx, calls clearTokens(), so a brief outage signs the user out. Only clear the tokens on a 401 from /auth/refresh.

issues: The fields are not cleared when the dialog is closed without saving (Escape or X); reopening shows the old values. Minor.

action_items: core.current_member: prefer the Authorization Bearer header over the cookie (or drop cookie auth now that the frontend uses Bearer tokens).
Production: set CORS_ORIGINS to explicit origins, or remove the cookie fallback to close the CSRF surface.
api.js: only clearTokens() when /auth/refresh returns 401, not on network or 5xx errors.
Optional: reset the Change password dialog fields when it closes; consider an admin unlock for per-email lockouts.
critical_code_review_comments: Verified fixed: _ip() no longer trusts X-Forwarded-For (7 spoofed-XFF attempts -> 401 x5 then 429); per-email lock row 'email:<addr>' is created; TTL index updated_at (86400s) exists; link-info and set-password return 400 for a deleted employee; login, set-password and change-password return access_token and refresh_token; /auth/refresh accepts the body and rejects access tokens and garbage.
The shared 'refreshing' promise in api.js correctly avoids parallel refresh storms.
Tokens in localStorage can be read by XSS; this is acceptable given the cross-host setup, but keep the CSP and dependency hygiene strict.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of requested auth flows on both hosts

seed_data_creation: Temporary: TEST_UI4 (UI test), TEST_FIX_<hex> / TEST_DEL_<hex> / TEST_AUTH_<hex> (pytest fixtures), plus their password_tokens and audit_logs. All deleted by id. login_attempts is empty at the end, so no unfiltered delete was needed. TEST_ADM/MGR/EMP passwords were not changed (password_version still 1). The owner and seed admin accounts were not touched.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: cd /app/backend && pytest tests/ (51 tests). Silent refresh must be tested on the 1c87 host (cross-site, so no cookies are sent); on the REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL host the same-origin cookie hides missing tokens. New employees see a monitoring-notice-dialog on first login: click acknowledge-notice-button before using the user menu.
